case_title: Selvamani v. The State Rep. By The Inspector of Police
statutory_provisions: IPC s.376(2)(g), s.506(1); Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act s.4
trial_court_outcome: Convicted under Sections 376(2)(g), 506(1) IPC and Section 4 of Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act
neutral_facts: The accused, who was the manager of a shoe company, allegedly gang-raped the victim, a female employee, while she was returning home after work. The victim reported the incident to the police, and an FIR was lodged on the same day. The victim's statement was recorded under Section 164 CrPC by a judicial magistrate. The medical expert confirmed the victim had injuries consistent with sexual assault. The trial court convicted the accused under Sections 376(2)(g) and 506(1) of the IPC and Section 4 of the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Woman Act. The accused appealed, arguing that the victim and her witnesses turned hostile during cross-examination. The Supreme Court upheld the conviction, noting that the victim's statement was corroborated by the FIR, the medical evidence, and the testimony of her mother and aunt.
